seo.title: 50 Portfolio Project Ideas for Smart Contract Auditors
seo.description: Build your security auditor portfolio with these 50 project ideas. From vulnerability databases to automated detection tools, showcase your expertise to potential clients.

content.intro: As a smart contract auditor, your portfolio needs to demonstrate deep security expertise and practical experience finding vulnerabilities. These project ideas will help you build credibility with protocols and audit firms.

sections.heading: Vulnerability Research Projects
sections.description: Document and analyze real-world exploits to demonstrate your understanding of attack vectors.

items.title: Exploit Post-Mortem Database
items.description: Create a searchable database of DeFi exploits with technical breakdowns, root cause analysis, and prevention strategies for each incident.

items.title: Reentrancy Pattern Catalog
items.description: Build a comprehensive catalog of reentrancy variations including cross-function, cross-contract, and read-only reentrancy with code examples.
outcomes: Shows mastery of common vulnerability class

items.title: Flash Loan Attack Simulator
items.description: Develop a tool that simulates flash loan attacks against test contracts to demonstrate various manipulation techniques.

items.title: Oracle Manipulation Lab
items.description: Create a testing environment demonstrating price oracle attacks including TWAP manipulation and spot price attacks.

items.title: Access Control Vulnerability Scanner
items.description: Build a static analysis tool that detects common access control issues like missing modifiers and privilege escalation paths.

sections.heading: Security Tooling Projects
sections.description: Build tools that automate or assist the audit process.

items.title: Custom Slither Detectors
items.description: Write custom Slither detectors for vulnerability patterns not covered by default rules, such as protocol-specific issues.

items.title: Foundry Fuzzing Framework
items.description: Create a reusable fuzzing framework with invariant tests for common DeFi primitives like AMMs, lending, and vaults.

items.title: Gas Griefing Detector
items.description: Build a tool that identifies potential gas griefing vulnerabilities in contracts with unbounded loops or external calls.

items.title: Upgrade Safety Checker
items.description: Develop a tool that validates proxy upgrade safety by checking storage layout compatibility and initialization patterns.

items.title: MEV Vulnerability Scanner
items.description: Create a scanner that identifies sandwich attack and frontrunning vulnerabilities in DeFi contracts.

sections.heading: CTF and Educational Content
sections.description: Create learning resources that demonstrate your teaching ability and deep understanding.

items.title: Custom CTF Challenge Set
items.description: Design a series of increasingly difficult smart contract CTF challenges covering various vulnerability classes.

items.title: Damn Vulnerable DeFi Solutions Guide
items.description: Write detailed walkthroughs for Damn Vulnerable DeFi challenges explaining the thought process and multiple solution approaches.

items.title: Security Pattern Cheatsheet
items.description: Create a visual cheatsheet of security patterns and anti-patterns with code examples and real exploit references.

items.title: Audit Report Template Library
items.description: Develop a library of audit report templates with standardized vulnerability descriptions and severity classifications.

items.title: Video Audit Walkthrough Series
items.description: Record video walkthroughs of your audit process on open-source contracts, explaining your methodology.

sections.heading: Real Protocol Analysis
sections.description: Analyze live protocols to demonstrate real-world auditing skills.

items.title: Public Audit of Small Protocol
items.description: Conduct a thorough public audit of a smaller protocol's contracts and publish your findings responsibly.

items.title: Protocol Comparison Analysis
items.description: Compare the security architecture of similar protocols (e.g., Aave vs Compound) highlighting design tradeoffs.

items.title: Bug Bounty Hunting Documentation
items.description: Document your bug bounty hunting process and findings (with permission) to show real vulnerability discovery.

items.title: Governance Attack Analysis
items.description: Analyze governance mechanisms of major DAOs for potential attack vectors like flash loan governance attacks.

items.title: Bridge Security Deep Dive
items.description: Conduct a thorough analysis of cross-chain bridge architectures and their historical vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Automation and Monitoring
sections.description: Build systems for ongoing security monitoring and automated checks.

items.title: Contract Monitoring Bot
items.description: Build a bot that monitors deployed contracts for suspicious transactions or state changes indicating exploitation.

items.title: Automated Audit Pipeline
items.description: Create a CI/CD pipeline that runs security tools (Slither, Mythril, custom checks) on every commit.

items.title: Exploit Alert System
items.description: Build a system that scrapes security feeds and alerts on new exploits relevant to protocols you're monitoring.

items.title: Storage Slot Monitor
items.description: Create a tool that monitors critical storage slots in contracts and alerts on unexpected changes.

items.title: Mempool Watcher for Attacks
items.description: Build a mempool monitoring tool that detects potential attack transactions before they're mined.

proTips.tip: Start with Code4rena contests to build a public track record of findings before pitching to protocols directly.
Document every finding in a personal database. Patterns you see once will appear again, and quick reference saves time.
Build relationships with protocol teams even when you don't find bugs. Reputation matters more than individual audits.
Specialize in one area deeply (bridges, lending, AMMs) before broadening. Deep expertise commands premium rates.
Always disclose responsibly. Never publish exploit details before the protocol has patched. Your reputation depends on trust.
